title: SLO Program Initiative: Error Budgeting, SLIs, and Release Gates
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Overview: Define and ship an initiative-grade SLO program that ties service-level indicators (SLIs) and error budgets into Redwood Console and the release rollout pipeline. The goal is to make reliability objectives actionable for PMs, SREs, and Platform engineers by: 1) standardizing SLI definitions across core inference services (api-gateway, runtime, kv-cache, batching); 2) configuring SLO targets and rolling error budgets with multiple burn-rate windows; 3) surfacing error budget status and burn alerts in Console dashboards; and 4) gating automated rollouts when error budgets are depleted.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI definitions documented for latency, p50/p95/p99, request success rate, and model response validity across hosted and dedicated modes
SLO targets and error budget windows configurable per-service in Console (example defaults: 99.9% monthly availability, 99.5% weekly for latency thresholds)
Error budget burn alerts with three severity levels (informational, action-required, rollout-block) delivered to Slack and visible in Console
Release gate hook implemented: automated canary/A-B rollouts paused when error budget enters rollout-block state and a runbook is surfaced
End-to-end demo showing a simulated error budget burn scenario that triggers alerting and pauses a canary rollout
metrics: Percentage of customer-facing services with canonical SLIs defined (target 100% of core services by due date)
Mean time to detect SLO breach (target < 5m for high-severity breaches)
Reduction in post-deploy incidents attributed to rollout-related reliability regressions (OKR target: 30% reduction)
Number of automated rollouts blocked by SLO gates (used as a guardrail metric)
risks: Ambiguity in SLI definitions across model types (chat vs batch embeddings) could cause noisy alerts
Overly aggressive rollout gates may slow feature delivery and cause product friction
Instrumentation gaps in Dedicated/Private deployments may prevent consistent SLI measurement
